title: What 6 months of AI game dev gets you making a national park simulator in three.js
author: idun0
selftext:
Hi! -This is "Switchback: a tiny hiking and park simulator" and I'm proud of this little game claude and I made through many many hundreds of hours of back and forth and iteration and even some minor manual coding design work on my end. It's cute, it's fun, it's dynamic, and it's what I've always wanted in a little diorama-y / building sim. It's been a joy to work on and wanted to share it.

This specifically is a comparison of my first month end of working with claude 20x and roughly 6 months later for the same level. I now have something like 30 levels and a few expansion packs as well.

More context - this game is kind of like Roller Coaster Tycoon but for National Parks. Theres a trail placing system, switchbacks, bridges, and lots of other stuff for management and maintenance. The general purpose is to solve little puzzles, create a world thats your own, and help your hikees reach viewpoints

Every map has a lot of world meta data to work with. Everything form height mapping and steepness and biome/subbiome and rock type, to wetness, temperature, wind affect, lat-long, and much more. I purposely pursued a huge number of world values because this is something that I feel is now far more manageable as a solo dev that ever before with the help of AI. and the results end up being fairly dynamic and delightful to play with. Things like getting certain types of butterflies to spawn only in their exact conditions in their exact season or migration path, etc. is all fairly trivial to add and adds a level of detail to appreciate. 

Its three.js and voxel based, most of my time has honestly been spent optimizing and building custom solutions to things that likely already exist or have been solved... but thats kind of the joy of these AI primary projects in my view, finding unique solutions to problems that are uniquely yours

If you'd like to give it a try its on both App Stores [https://apps.apple.com/us/app/switchback-a-cozy-hiking-game/id6799833310](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/switchback-a-cozy-hiking-game/id6799833310) and [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.swanklabs.switchback](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.swanklabs.switchback).

https://reddit.com/link/1xg3bc9/video/2uyk58y7iuxh1/player

You can tell me it's slop if you'd like, But I'd like to think it's more of a bisque or warm broth though at this point.

if you have a windows PC or Mac, try out the desk top versions of the apps because it works best with mouse and keyboard. iPad is also good and then phone is ok, but it certainly takes a little more effort and doesn't look quite as good.

If you have any questions I would love to discuss and will be in the comments :) would also love more feedback before I put on steam! I'm particularly proud of my asset process and map process.

coming soon are more activities like rafting and paragliding :)

comments.author: cheyumaama
comments.body: I think it looked better at 1 month unless I'm tripping

replies.author: idun0
replies.body: I should have used a clear day to compare it to so it was more 1-1 - but to be yeah... I kind of miss more cellshaded  look. maybe I'll start pushing back that direction.

comments.author: liright
comments.body: In the 6 month version, why have that fake 2D boundary? Why not extend the actual 3D trees into the distance, maybe make them lower res and lower polygon for performance? It would look 100x better.

replies.author: idun0
replies.body:
I'll have give it a try! I haven't really played around with extending the world like that yet.  
  
Honestly I've just kept it because liked the diorama look to it and performance has been easy to manage with it. The panorama pieces cost almost nothing and are easy to work with for things like sunsets/lighting/updates to like world values like snow and fog.  They also do a good job at hiding funky transitions and at the edge of the world.

also it looks good in first person mode to trick the eyes with a kind of parallax in the distance.

replies.author: idun0
replies.body: or maybe its a mix of both? like extend world out to those edges and gradually reduce size until its matching the size of those 2d bands? so it looks like one continuous world with faux big mountains still in the distance? that could be cool.
